evidence.exact_quote: only one attachment may hold mutation-capable focus at a time

items.impact: Independent implementations can accept invalid transitions, permit competing writers, or strand mutation authority after partial failure.
items.statement: The prologue fixes lifecycle states and a single mutation-capable attachment but does not define the allowed transition graph, atomic focus-transfer protocol, stale-holder fencing, or recovery when the focused attachment crashes.
items.title: Preview lifecycle and focus transitions are under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: - **Full HTML/browser mode** uses a loopback localhost preview server rooted to the workspace/project context.

items.impact: A hostile local process or crafted workspace path could reach preview content or privileges inconsistently, and builders lack a falsifiable security oracle.
items.statement: The loopback preview server is named, but host binding, per-session authentication, origin checks, path-traversal containment, port collision behavior, and shutdown/recovery are not specified here.
items.title: Loopback HTML preview trust boundary lacks a wire-level security contract

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master uses one deterministic agent loop with every backend as a Provider behind a unified session/event store, tool registry, and patch/edit pipeline, adapting OpenCode architecture without CLI-bridged special-case chaos.

items.impact: This gives builders a clear ownership baseline and prevents duplicate provider execution stacks.
items.statement: RTIM-002 unambiguously centralizes providers, events, tools, and edits behind one agent-loop spine and prohibits CLI-specific architecture forks.
items.title: Unified Provider spine is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The node graph is the canonical execution model; Feature Seam, Work Package, Node, promotion states, governance overseers, graph generation lineage, route_target, and OpenSubject stay locked as rewrite-era orchestration canon.

items.impact: Racey graph publication can split execution and GUI consumers across generations or let governance roles accidentally act as schedulers.
items.statement: RTIM-003 names canonical graph objects and lineage but does not state who may publish a generation, how concurrent graph patches are serialized, when a generation becomes effective, or how consumers reject stale generations.
items.title: Graph-generation authority needs mutation semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator remains tab-first with Progress, Plan Compile, Seams, Node Graph, Evidence, History, and Ledger; Progress is the only widget-composed tab, while Plan Compile and the other non-Progress Orchestrator tabs are native-purpose surfaces.

items.impact: This prevents implementation from silently turning native-purpose tabs into generic widget canvases.
items.statement: RTIM-004 clearly fixes tab inventory and makes Progress the sole widget-composed surface.
items.title: Orchestrator surface boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Desktop UI uses Rust plus Slint with winit plus Skia by default, FemtoVG-wgpu fallback, emergency software fallback, restart-acceptable theme switching, and no stale Iced path.

items.impact: Different builds can fall back at different failures and hide degraded rendering, complicating support and compatibility diagnosis.
items.statement: RTIM-005 locks the renderer order but does not define health probes, fallback triggers, persistence of the effective renderer, user disclosure, or recovery back to the preferred renderer.
items.title: Renderer fallback selection is not operationally defined

evidence.exact_quote: Persistence is seglog as the canonical append-only event ledger, redb for durable KV projections/settings, and Tantivy search; replay, checkpoint, rebuild, analytics, runs, sessions, artifacts, annotations, and dashboards route through storage-plan ownership.

items.impact: A rebuild can silently diverge from live projections while still satisfying the PlanUnit's generic validation surfaces.
items.statement: RTIM-006 fixes store roles and ownership but its local acceptance criteria only preserve migration shape; it does not state checkpoint atomicity, projector idempotency, corruption behavior, or byte-for-byte/semantic replay equivalence.
items.title: Replay and projection determinism lack executable invariants

evidence.exact_quote: Tools flow through central policy and normalized result governance, while edits use explicit patch, apply, verify, and rollback paths aligned with worktree/branch/sandbox safety and FileSafe intent.

items.impact: This prevents direct destructive writes from becoming a parallel normal path.
items.statement: RTIM-007 clearly requires centrally governed tool results and an explicit patch/apply/verify/rollback path for edits.
items.title: Central tool and patch governance boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Claude Code CLI and Cursor Agent CLI are bridged Providers using machine-readable streams; Cursor CLI is not ACP-native, so ACP needs a PM-side adapter instead of assuming native Cursor ACP support.

items.impact: Provider bridges can emit inconsistent unified events or duplicate side effects after interruption.
items.statement: RTIM-008 fixes stream formats and the ACP boundary but not malformed-frame handling, ordering, duplicate suppression, process death, backpressure, cancellation acknowledgement, or restart-from-durable-boundary behavior.
items.title: CLI stream failure and resumption semantics are absent

evidence.exact_quote: Gemini Direct gemini and Gemini CLI gemini_cli are separate provider entries; OAuth, API key, and Google/Vertex credentials are distinct auth surfaces and quota planes, and stale mixed-provider Gemini canon is retired.

items.impact: This blocks misleading account pooling and cross-plane authority assumptions.
items.statement: RTIM-009 precisely separates provider entries, credential surfaces, and quota planes and retires the mixed-provider model.
items.title: Gemini auth-plane separation is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Requested and effective Gemini auth/account identity must be visible across prompt assembly, storage, setup/health, usage, media capabilities, runtime reporting, and anti-key-centric GUI copy.

items.impact: GUI implementations may display a resolved-looking identity when resolution is stale or failed, misleading users about quota and billing authority.
items.statement: RTIM-010 requires visibility across consumers but does not define pending, stale, unavailable, permission-denied, or unknown-source presentation, nor accessible/localizable labels and mismatch actions.
items.title: Requested/effective identity GUI states are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: Mobile and web clients are thin clients that consume streamed events/artifacts and send commands to the desktop-owned core; they must not call providers, tool executors, or local patch pipelines directly.

items.impact: A remote client could replay destructive commands, miss approvals, or observe artifacts outside its authority while still conforming to the stated boundary.
items.statement: RTIM-011 defines the authority boundary but not client authentication, authorization scopes, command idempotency, replay cursors, reconnect ordering, revocation, or offline queue rejection.
items.title: Thin-client command channel omits trust, idempotency, and offline behavior

evidence.exact_quote: Implementation targets Provider terminology, unified event model, Provider trait, tool registry, and event-sourced seglog to redb/Tantivy session storage, without SQLite alternatives or platform-runner vocabulary forks.

items.impact: This provides a clear implementation vocabulary and storage boundary.
items.statement: RTIM-012 fixes the interfaces and explicitly rejects SQLite and platform-runner forks.
items.title: Implementation interfaces and forbidden forks are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: UI updates must cross the Slint event-loop boundary, and Settings/config/provider invocation must not expose per-platform experimental settings, experimentalEnabled keys, or provider-side experimental toggles for runtime behavior.

items.impact: This prevents hidden polling paths and unstable capability exposure.
items.statement: RTIM-013 clearly requires event-loop delivery and prohibits experimental controls across UI, config, and invocation.
items.title: Slint event-loop and experimental-toggle prohibition is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Assistant memory is Assistant-only continuity; Gist generation is artifact-driven and must not alter Provider spine contracts, unified event model ownership, or shared rules pipeline semantics.

items.impact: This guards against a continuity subsystem becoming hidden runtime authority.
items.statement: RTIM-014 explicitly limits assistant memory and artifact-driven gists from taking over provider, event, or rules ownership.
items.title: Assistant memory authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: Rewrite reconciliation must retire stale Gemini mixed-provider wording, Codex/Copilot CLI-provider language, OpenCode server/cli_launcher framing, provider-native skill/MCP ownership, and Cursor --user-data-dir canon.

items.impact: This gives reconciliation a concrete negative register instead of relying on interpretation.
items.statement: RTIM-015 enumerates the stale concepts that must be retired across documents.
items.title: Stale provider canon retirement is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Older flat bottom-terminal strip, single editor dock slot, and separate command-log strip assumptions are retired in favor of workgroups, subtabs, split-pane trees, multi-panel editor terminal stack, and explicit DnD semantics.

items.impact: This reduces GUI ambiguity and prevents parallel layout canon.
items.statement: RTIM-016 explicitly retires the old terminal/editor layout and names the replacement concepts.
items.title: Terminal and editor compatibility disposition is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Rewrite-aware edits must land in the owning docs for browser, debug, runtime, prompt, tool, storage, and GUI deltas before mirrors; newfeatures.md remains historical origin material only.

items.impact: The memo can claim reconciliation while an owner or mirror remains stale, and the generic migration validators need not detect semantic drift.
items.statement: RTIM-017 says owner docs must be updated before mirrors, but does not define a machine-checkable owner-to-mirror register, completion receipt, stale-mirror detector, or failure disposition.
items.title: Cross-document reconciliation has no closure receipt

evidence.exact_quote: Provider contracts, unified event model, tool registry, and patch pipeline stay owner-first; chat tool cards, /diff, Mermaid, and thread Context Detail Pane behavior route through owning chat, GUI, and usage contracts.

items.impact: This avoids chat-local reinvention of tool, diff, diagram, and context contracts.
items.statement: RTIM-018 keeps backend contracts owner-first and routes chat/rendering surfaces to their consumers.
items.title: Owner-first chat and rendering routes are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Rendering uses one Slint shell, native Rust document core, and isolated preview/browser runtime across chat, editor, embedded panes, detached previews, and browser surfaces, while source text or file bytes remain canonical.

items.impact: This prevents DOM or preview state from becoming a hidden second source of truth.
items.statement: RTIM-019 fixes one rendering architecture and preserves source bytes/text as the authority across surfaces.
items.title: Unified source-canonical rendering architecture is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Preview subjects are doc:<document_id> or artifact:<artifact_id>; required artifact metadata and preview_subject_id provide stable restore, UI-state, and audit joins for document-backed and artifact-backed previews.

items.impact: Artifact-backed content can become undeletable, cross-thread visible, or incorrectly restored after partial persistence.
items.statement: RTIM-020 defines identity shape but not ID generation/collision handling, retention and deletion, access control, redaction, orphan cleanup, or behavior when an artifact-document link becomes stale.
items.title: Artifact identity lifecycle is under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: open_source opens real doc buffers for doc:* and transient generated://<artifact_id> source buffers for artifact:* until Save As or Insert into file creates the first stable workspace path.

items.impact: Save As can leave a file and artifact identity diverged or cause an unintended overwrite without a canonical recovery path.
items.statement: RTIM-021 defines the transition from transient artifact to stable file but not atomicity when file creation succeeds and linkage fails, collision/overwrite prompts, cancellation, rollback, or retry idempotency.
items.title: First-persist linking lacks partial-failure semantics

evidence.exact_quote: OpenSubject resolves doc/artifact identity before path realization; OpenFile path form is only for already-known real files, and resume_url is serialization/restore rather than hidden route canon.

items.impact: This prevents paths and deep links from silently replacing durable subject identity.
items.statement: RTIM-022 clearly makes identity resolution canonical, confines OpenFile to real known paths, and makes resume_url transport-only.
items.title: Identity-native routing boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Reviewer deltas, projection health, minority_advisory, runtime-artifact schema registration, source-open resolver rules, and provider recovery controls must move to owner docs rather than remain memo-only observations.

items.impact: Important deltas can remain memo-only indefinitely while the PlanUnit itself appears accepted.
items.statement: RTIM-023 identifies obligations that must move to owner docs but does not define assignment state, rejection/disposition rules, completion evidence, or how unresolved obligations block downstream use.
items.title: Owner-routing obligations have no due-state or acceptance protocol

evidence.exact_quote: PreviewSession tracks rendered subject identity and lifecycle states while browser-capable surfaces layer browser_session_id, session_class, automation, auth, evidence, route, focus, and recovery identity without collapsing them into generic preview instances.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on invalid transitions and leak or resurrect browser/automation state.
items.statement: RTIM-024 names state and identity layers but does not define legal transitions, terminal/reopen behavior, stale-to-ready rules, error/degraded precedence, or correlated browser-session teardown.
items.title: PreviewSession states lack an allowed-transition matrix

evidence.exact_quote: Preview attachment targets are chat_card, editor_preview, embedded_doc_pane, editor_browser_tab, and detached_window; bottom_panel_browser is noncanonical and only one attachment holds mutation-capable focus at a time.

items.impact: Two surfaces can believe they own mutation focus or leave users unable to edit after a crashed holder.
items.statement: RTIM-025 fixes a single mutation-capable focus holder but not acquisition, transfer, timeout, stale-holder fencing, user takeover, or UI behavior during simultaneous requests.
items.title: Mutation-capable focus needs fencing and takeover rules

evidence.exact_quote: The app persists preview intent, attachment target, visible errors, lifecycle changes, and overlay state sufficient for restore/audit, but it does not persist live DOM state or browser storage as PreviewSession state.

items.impact: Restore can pair incompatible identities or hide stale audit state after a crash or migration.
items.statement: RTIM-026 defines persisted fields and prohibited live state but not transaction boundaries, schema migration, corrupt-record handling, projector lag disclosure, or consistency between preview and browser overlays.
items.title: Restore projections lack consistency and corruption behavior

evidence.exact_quote: Generated previews use pm-preview://session/<preview_session_id>/ with app-controlled assets, restrictive CSP, sanitized Markdown-derived HTML, required source-mapping metadata attributes, and no arbitrary remote script/cookie reuse.

items.impact: Crafted Markdown could smuggle misleading mapping or capability metadata into privileged bridge requests unless authority is recomputed from trusted host state.
items.statement: RTIM-027 requires sanitization and source-mapping attributes but does not state that host authorization must ignore content-supplied capability claims, define exact CSP directives, validate attribute values, or fail closed when parsing/sanitization disagrees.
items.title: Preview bridge metadata trust is not closed

evidence.exact_quote: Generated-preview bridge v1 exposes only open_source, open_detached, request_edit, export_svg, export_png, copy_svg, and copy_image; no other host command family is implicitly available.

items.impact: This sharply bounds generated-content authority.
items.statement: RTIM-028 provides a closed v1 bridge allowlist and explicitly denies implicit host command families.
items.title: Generated preview host-command allowlist is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical rendering stack uses pulldown-cmark, syntect, ammonia, Mermaid validation, and resvg/usvg/tiny-skia; generated previews, visual modules, and full HTML/browser mode remain separate trust tiers.

items.impact: A dependency update can change parsing, sanitization, or export output without a controlled compatibility or security response.
items.statement: RTIM-029 chooses libraries and trust tiers but does not pin compatible versions, define security update cadence, specify sanitizer regression gates, or declare rollback behavior for rendering dependency upgrades.
items.title: Rendering dependencies lack version and vulnerability policy

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master owns a PM-managed pinned bundled CEF-class Chromium runtime, including version/cache/integrity/rollback/offline install policy, multi-process, sandbox, codec, PDF, DevTools, platform layout, and atomic update behavior.

items.impact: Updates can exhaust disk, race live browser processes, or leave an apparently verified but unusable runtime without deterministic recovery.
items.statement: RTIM-030 lists required bundle concerns but not free-space preflight, concurrent running-session behavior, lock ownership, rollback trigger, cleanup of old bundles, or measurable atomicity checks.
items.title: CEF bundle update transaction lacks concurrency and capacity bounds

evidence.exact_quote: Browser surfaces use editor-tab primary hosting plus first-class detached windows on one PM browser model; degraded UX must disclose runtime_unavailable, preserve source/native surfaces, and reject blank panes or screenshot-only substitution as steady state.

items.impact: Users retain an honest usable fallback rather than a fake live browser.
items.statement: RTIM-031 clearly requires runtime_unavailable disclosure, preserves source/native routes, and rejects misleading blank or screenshot-only steady states.
items.title: Browser degraded-state GUI contract is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Doctor/setup validates bundled browser runtime presence, expected version, startup health, editor-tab host, and detached host before browser capability is advertised.

items.impact: Doctor implementations can report healthy using incompatible probes and leave capability state stale.
items.statement: RTIM-032 enumerates check subjects but not timeouts, pass/fail thresholds, diagnostic evidence, cache invalidation, repair action, or capability re-advertisement after remediation.
items.title: Doctor checks lack pass thresholds and remediation outcomes

evidence.exact_quote: Preview mutations resolve to canonical text patches, validate node_id, parse_revision and source_revision, stay inside mapped source spans, and fail with deterministic result codes for stale revisions, unsupported regions, or ambiguous mappings.

items.impact: Concurrent editor and preview edits can apply a patch to the wrong text while each local validation step appears correct.
items.statement: RTIM-033 requires revision validation and bounded spans but does not explicitly require atomic compare-and-apply against the shared buffer or define behavior when the buffer changes after validation but before mutation.
items.title: Preview patch validation is vulnerable to validation-apply races

evidence.exact_quote: Successful preview edits update the shared buffer, dirty state, undo/redo history, and preview revision; failures focus source where possible and show deterministic user-facing reasons.

items.impact: Users may see a failed preview while an edit committed, or undo an unrelated concurrent change.
items.statement: RTIM-034 defines successful side effects and failure presentation but not ordering with concurrent editor edits, undo behavior after remote changes, focus failure, or whether partial downstream rerender failure rolls back the buffer.
items.title: Undo and failure UI need concurrent-edit semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Selection actions such as comment, replace, insert_after, remove, and send_selection_to_chat create annotations or document_selection_context attachments and are not direct preview mutations unless wired to the validated patch path.

items.impact: Selections can leak into unauthorized chats or persist after source deletion, and destructive annotation actions can diverge from source state.
items.statement: RTIM-035 separates annotation from mutation but does not define who may create/read/delete annotations, retention/redaction, stale-anchor behavior, destination-thread authorization, or sensitive-selection handling.
items.title: Annotation lifecycle and authorization are unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: Markdown uses Rust parser/mapping and sanitized HTML, while Mermaid remains text-canonical from fenced mermaid blocks or .mmd files, is validated before render, exports SVG as canonical render artifact, and derives PNG from SVG rasterization.

items.impact: This prevents a hidden diagram object model and makes export provenance coherent.
items.statement: RTIM-036 clearly preserves text as Mermaid authority, validates before rendering, and defines SVG-to-PNG derivation.
items.title: Markdown and Mermaid source authority is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The rendering contract has no requirement for identical embedded browser panes on every platform, arbitrary WYSIWYG DOM editing, hidden diagram state, or a full-privilege host bridge shared between generated preview content and arbitrary workspace HTML.

items.impact: This bounds builder discretion without forcing unsafe cross-platform equivalence.
items.statement: RTIM-037 clearly excludes WYSIWYG DOM authority, hidden diagram state, cross-tier full privilege, and identical platform embedding.
items.title: Rendering non-goals and privilege prohibitions are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime scheduler updates are event-driven; queue analysis, remediation lineage, safe points, and projector state derive from canonical event/projection state, with safe points distinct from user-facing restore/rollback history.

items.impact: Schedulers can resume from a boundary that projections have not durably agreed on or duplicate remediation after restart.
items.statement: RTIM-038 establishes event-driven ownership and separates safe points from user history, but does not define safe-point creation/commit validity, projector lag handling, retry races, or recovery after a partially emitted remediation lineage.
items.title: Scheduler safe points and blocked projections lack transition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked outcomes remain first-class in rewrite-era UI and storage and must not be flattened into generic failures.

items.impact: UI and storage can use incompatible meanings for blocked, strand recoverable work, or falsely present a temporary block as terminal.
items.statement: RTIM-039 preserves blocked as distinct from failure, but does not define blocked reason taxonomy, entry/exit transitions, retry/unblock authority, persistence schema, user actions, or terminal-vs-temporary presentation. The remaining generated bridge and migration/addendum lines do not add those runtime semantics.
items.title: Blocked outcome state is preserved but not behaviorally defined

segments.summary: Reviewed lines 1-348 exactly and adversarially. The architecture and trust split are extensive, but PreviewSession lifecycle and mutation-focus transition mechanics remain under-specified.

Reviewed lines 349-557 and all ten assigned semantic/PlanUnit bindings. Provider, storage, GUI, auth, rendering, and patch boundaries are present; key gaps concern loopback trust, graph publication, replay, stream failure, renderer fallback, and honest identity states.

Reviewed lines 558-647 and every RTIM-011 through RTIM-025 binding. Strong owner and identity boundaries coexist with missing thin-client wire security, handoff closure, artifact lifecycle, first-persist recovery, PreviewSession transitions, and focus fencing.

Reviewed lines 648-725 and every RTIM-026 through RTIM-038 binding. Explicit preview security, bridge, browser, patch, annotation, rendering, and scheduler contracts were tested against races, partial failure, lifecycle, and operational oracles; the reported gaps are the unresolved negative space.

Reviewed lines 726-852, including RTIM-039 and the retired bridge, migration proof tail, and deferred-action addendum. Only RTIM-039 is an assigned source unit; tail material is routing/migration lineage and does not close the blocked-state behavioral gap.

cross_document_questions: Do storage-plan and the runtime contracts define one allowed PreviewSession and browser-session transition matrix with atomic focus transfer and stale-holder fencing?
Do Contracts_V0 and the thin-client API owner define authenticated, authorized, idempotent commands plus replay cursors, reconnect ordering, and revocation?
Do FileManager and FileSafe require atomic compare-and-apply for preview patches and transactionally couple first file persist to artifact-document linkage?
Do Permissions_System and UI_Command_Catalog recompute preview bridge authority from trusted host state rather than content-supplied data-pm-capabilities?
Do Orchestrator and storage owners define blocked reason taxonomy, unblock authority, persistence, and terminal-versus-retryable GUI states?
research_queries: Official CEF guidance for atomic runtime bundle updates, multi-process shutdown, sandboxing, and cross-platform integrity verification
Official Slint guidance for renderer fallback detection, event-loop delivery, and effective backend diagnostics
Security guidance for authenticated loopback preview servers, strict CSP, origin validation, and local-process threat models
Distributed command API patterns for idempotency keys, replay cursors, reconnect ordering, and offline rejection
Property-based and model-based testing patterns for preview lifecycle transitions and atomic revision compare-and-apply
